statements.status_notes: The vulnerability is in oras-go's content/file tar-extraction helper (ensureLinkPath), reached only when a content/file Store extracts an OCI artifact carrying the unpack annotation. kubescape does not use oras-go in its own source; the module enters the graph only indirectly through helm.sh/helm/v3, whose sole oras usage is its registry client (content/memory plus registry/remote). Neither kubescape nor helm imports oras-go's content/file package, so the vulnerable extraction path is never linked or invoked. Both the 3.x and 4.x lines ship oras-go 2.6.1.

The vulnerability is in oras-go's content/file tar-extraction helper (ensureLinkPath), reached only when a content/file Store extracts an OCI artifact carrying the unpack annotation. This image ships two Go binaries and neither reaches that path. The fleetconfig-controller manager binary does not link oras-go at all (it is absent from that module's graph). The bundled clusteradm binary pulls oras-go only indirectly through helm.sh/helm/v3, whose sole oras usage is its registry client (content/memory plus registry/remote); neither helm, clusteradm, nor the Open Cluster Management libraries import oras-go's content/file package. The vulnerable extraction path is therefore never linked or invoked.

Zot now bumps oras.land/oras-go/v2 to v2.6.1, the latest available v2 module release, which addresses the other open oras-go advisories. CVE-2026-50163 is still reported as affecting oras-go through v2.6.1, and no newer v2 module release is currently available. Reachability through Zot's ORAS artifact handling is still under investigation.
